# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**6:1** And-you know that no treachery or deceit or evil is-found in-our-hand, since for [these matters] we give [...]

**6:2** [...] and-indeed we write to-you [...] for-your-good and-for-the-good of-your-people [...]

**6:3** [...] for we saw that-you-have wisdom and-knowledge of-the-Torah. Consider [...]

**6:4** [...] all the-things that come-upon-you [...] and-you-will-find [...]

**6:5** [And in]deed we have [written] to-you some of-the-works of-the-Torah which we-think are-good for-you and for-your-people, for we-saw that-you-have wisdom and-knowledge of-the-Torah.

**6:6** Consider all these-things and-ask from-Him that-He-straighten your counsel and-keep far from-you evil scheming and-the-counsel of-Belial,

**6:7** so-that you-may-rejoice at-the-end of-time when-you-find that some of-our-words are-true.

**6:8** And-it-will-be-reckoned to-you as-righteousness when-you-do what-is-right and-good before-Him, for-your-good and-for-the-good of-Israel.

**6:9** [...] for [...] in the book of-Moses it-is-written [...] and-in the words of-the-prophets [...]

**6:10** [...] that the blessings have-come [...] in-the-days-of Solomon the son-of-David [...] and-also the curses [...]

**6:11** [...] that have-come from-the-days-of Jeroboam the son-of-Nebat and-unto the exile of-Jerusalem and-of-Zedekiah king of-Judah [...]

**6:12** [...] that He-will-bring them [...] and-it is written [...] in the book of-Moses and-in-the-[words of-the]-prophets that [...]

**6:13** [...] [the bles]sings came in-the-days of-David and-Solomon [...] and-the-curses came from [...] unto [...]

**6:14** [...] and-we recognize that some of-the-blessings and-the-curses that-are-written in-the-book of-[Moses] have-come [...]

**6:15** and-this is the end of-days when-they-will-return in-Israel for-[ever ...] and-will-not turn back [...]

**6:16** [...] but-the-wicked will-act [...] and [...] remember [...]

**6:17** Remember the kings of-Israel and-contemplate their deeds: whoever among-them feared [the To]rah was-delivered from troubles;

**6:18** those were the seekers of-the-Torah whose transgressions were-forgiven.

**6:19** Remember David, who was a man of-pious-deeds, and-he too was-delivered from many troubles and-was-forgiven.

**6:20** And-also we have-written to-you some of-the-works of-the-Torah [...] that-it-should-be for-your-good [...]

**6:21** [...] for [...] you-shall-receive [...] at-the-end-of-time [...] when-you-walk in-uprightness before-Him [...]

**6:22** [...] and-it-will-be-reckoned to-you as-righteousness [...] for doing what-is-upright and-good before-Him [...]

**6:23** [...] for-your-good and-for-the-good of-Israel [...]

**6:24** [...] and-it is written: [...] at-the-end of-days [...]

**6:25** [...] and-remember all the-words of-Moses the servant of-God [...]

---

*EMET notes: Section C is the rhetorical climax of MMT. "It will be reckoned to you as righteousness" (6:8, 6:22) echoes Gen 15:6 (Abraham) and is the key phrase linking this text to Pauline theology — Paul's discussion of "works of the law" (erga nomou) in Galatians and Romans may directly engage this sectarian concept. "Counsel of Belial" uses the cosmic-adversary figure prominent in Qumran theology. The historical examples — Solomon's blessings, Jeroboam's curses, Zedekiah's exile — provide a deuteronomistic framework. David as "a man of pious deeds" (chasidei ma'asim) whose transgressions were forgiven alludes to the Bathsheba episode. Hyphenated forms preserve Hebrew construct chains. The document ends with an appeal to covenant faithfulness.*
